items.title: OpenAI is betting on giant compute
items.oneliner: OpenAI's Ohio campus targets nearly 8 GW of compute. Frontier progress now depends as much on power as models.

items.title: Alibaba pushed open models onto laptops
items.oneliner: Alibaba's laptop-ready open model raises the floor again. Local inference is becoming practical, not just ideological.

items.title: DuckDB is moving toward server mode
items.oneliner: DuckDB 2.0 adds networked access, async I/O, and a new parser. The embedded analytics darling is growing up.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly cut its risk team
items.oneliner: OpenAI reportedly disbanded Preparedness. Capability acceleration keeps winning internal arguments over catastrophic risk governance.

items.title: AI autofix introduced a CI exploit
items.oneliner: Wiz found an unauthenticated GitHub Actions exploit in Snowflake's Jira flow. AI-generated fixes are now a supply-chain risk.

items.title: State actors are targeting chatbot memory
items.oneliner: A fake think tank appears built to influence chatbot outputs. LLM poisoning is shifting from theory to geopolitical tactic.

items.title: ByteDance accepted Hollywood AI guardrails
items.oneliner: ByteDance struck formal AI video guardrails with the MPA. Copyright enforcement is getting operational, not rhetorical.

items.title: Cursor launched code hosting during GitHub trouble
items.oneliner: Cursor launched Origin as GitHub suffered a six-hour outage. AI coding tools are climbing the stack fast.

items.title: Google bought an airline's data exhaust
items.oneliner: Google paid $10 million for Spirit's deidentified records. Proprietary training data is becoming a strategic asset class.

items.title: Benchmarks are getting easier to game
items.oneliner: Dan Luu argues LLMs make benchmark gaming trivial. Reported wins matter less without serious auditing and eval design.
